newsitem.title: UK: Triplex steeled to lift Cook bid by 30 pct.
newsitem.headline: Triplex steeled to lift Cook bid by 30 pct.

text.p: A hostile bid by engineers Triplex Lloyd Plc for metal castings specialist William Cook Plc is almost certain to fail and is likely to be raised to about 400p per share from its current 309p, analysts said on Monday.
However, they also cautioned that Triplex would be well advised to avoid being enticed into overbidding for Cook, given the uncertainties many observers see over its future prospects.
"A higher price is inevitable," said John Dean, an analyst specialising in engineering stocks and smaller companies at Birmingham-based stockbrokers Albert E Sharp.
But he added: "It is debatable whether or not they should bid over 400p."

Triplex's bid, based on seven of its own shares and 1350p in cash for every nine William Cook shares, has been worth a fairly steady 309p since its launch in the middle of November. That means it values the entire castings firm at just under 58 million pounds ($97 million).

Meanwhile, William Cook shares, which stood at 240p the day before Triplex unveiled the bid, have risen -- first in a quick spurt to 320p and then more gradually to nearer 360p. In this time holders of just 0.39 percent of William Cook's capital have accepted the offer, the remainder opting to wait and see.
Analysts said this response reflects widespread anticipation that Triplex will raise their bid, yet several said it remained unclear what would constitute a fair price.
"I don't think shareholders should get their hopes up too high," an analyst at a London-based brokerage said.
"The first bid is dead in the water, but after Cook's vigorous defence there is a danger Triplex may get drawn into paying too much to satisfy some very demanding shareholders."
He also saw a revised bid being likely to home in on about 400p, valuing William Cook at nearer 75 million pounds.

Some analysts have calculated that a value that fully reflects William Cook's inherent earnings power would be about 550p, especially as the company has produced a glowing forecast of its prospects for earnings in its the current trading year.

However, a number of others say the company's mixed record over the past few years, and the fact that it has made very positive earnings noises only since the launch of Triplex's bid, justify a continued discount to its peers.

As well as the problems of valuing a small company like William Cook, analysts said, making judgements on a takeover price could also be influenced by sentiment about the level at which key shareholders are prepared to part with their stock.

Once again 400p is a critical point, some said, not necessarily due to any exacting financial valuation but because certain large shareholders appeared to have marked it out as a minimum selling level during informal contacts with brokers.

Adding extra uncertainty, the strict timetable for the entire bidding process under London's takeover code has been suspended since the end of December pending the conclusion of a monopolies review into the effect of the two firms combining.

While analysts and market players estimate that a mergers ruling should be given within a few weeks, Triplex Lloyd will be able to leave its tactical decision on when and how to pitch a raised bid until nine days after any such clearance is given. ($1=.5974 Pound)
